newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics ramps up, analysts wary.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics ramps up, analysts wary.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc executives said they have prepared the path for increasing growth in the second half of its fiscal year, but some analysts said they remain cautious after recent stumbles.

"Personally, I'm going to be a non-beleiver until I can see it to believe it," one analyst said, noting the company's recent spate of shortfalls. "It's a back-end loaded year and they have a lot to prove."
Silicon Graphics Chief Executive Edward McCracken said in a statement the company was disappointed with its net loss after special charges of $22 million, or $0.33 a share.

But he also said the company's customers had been "extremely enthusiastic" over its wide-ranging product launch ten days ago, which ranged from powerful $6,000 desktop models to highly scalable departmental servers and supercomputers.
Gary Lauer, president of Silicon Graphics Worlwide Trade Corp, said the product launch was its biggest in three years.
Lauer said it was still too early to provide quantitive details on the success of the launch. "Obviously the next few months are the proof of the pudding," he said.
Analysts described the product lineup as attractive, but said financial performance would require solid execution.

Lauer said the current, December quarter is "definitely a ramp-up quarter, with new technologies we've got to ramp up manufacturing and we're ramping up our sales force now we're getting the message to customers."
"We expect a very healthy order rate as a result of these product announcements," he said.

Stanley Moresman, SGI's senior vice president of finance and chief financial officer, said the company expects to start producing "significant growth" in year over year revenue figures in the second half of the 1997 fiscal year.
Moresman said the company's first quarter special writeoffs include "the $15 million charge for increasing the inventory reserves, primarily due to the new products."

A $10 million charge covered the costs of a program announced last month to replace R10000 microprocessor boards after some were found to have manufacturing flaws, while merger-related charges related to its acquisition of Cray Research amounted to around $21 million in charges.
Prior to the one-time charges, the company posted first quarter operating profit of $18 million, or $0.07 a share.
